[[File:History of the Theory of Numbers, 3 volumes.jpg|right|thumb|By Chelsa publishing]]
'''''History of the Theory of Numbers''''' is a three-volume work by [[Leonard Eugene Dickson]]  summarizing work in [[number theory]] up to about 1920. The style is unusual in that Dickson mostly just lists results by various authors, with little further discussion. The central topic of [[quadratic reciprocity]] and higher [[reciprocity law]]s is barely mentioned; this was apparently going to be the topic of a fourth volume that was never written {{harv|Fenster|1999}}.

==Volumes==
* Volume 1 - [[Divisibility]] and [[Primality]] - 486 pages
* Volume 2 - [[Diophantine equation|Diophantine Analysis]] - 803 pages
* Volume 3 - [[Quadratic form|Quadratic]] and Higher Forms - 313 pages
